text: Grandfather here, looking after my grandson aged 9 while his parents are abroad. Temperature this evening is 39.7°C, checked twice with a digital thermometer under the arm. His eczema has flared up badly at the same time – dry, rough patches on the backs of his knees and inside his elbows, and he's scratching at them constantly. I've put his usual cream on, the one his mother left. I'm not after a long chat. What I need to know is plain and simple: is 39.7 a number that means I take him somewhere tonight, or do I give him something for the fever and see how he is at breakfast? And is there anything else I should be doing for the skin beyond the cream? I'd rather be told straight.
